chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The witness is the Day of Arafah.

key_terms.وَمَشْهُود: And what is to be witnessed

ai.seo_question: What does the 'witness' in Surah Al-Buruj refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Maani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the 'witness' in Surah Al-Buruj as the Day of Arafah, a day of profound divine testimony and gathering. This identification underscores the unique status of Arafah in Shia eschatology as a pivotal moment where Allah’s presence and judgment are most manifest, linking the Quranic oath to the spiritual gravity of the Hajj pilgrimage.
